title: Practice 6: под- and от-: up to, and away from

blocks.text: Exercises: sentences from Tatoeba (tatoeba.org, CC BY 2.0 FR) and from the library's public-domain books.

exercises.q: Постоянные приграничные конфликты между Англией и Шотландией ___ (подойти / подходить) к концу.
exercises.why: Verbs of motion with the prefix под- denote approaching to an object, a place or a person and require the preposition к + dative case: Я подхожу к столу. Рядовой подходит к сержанту. — DLI, Lesson 29.  ·  Sentence and translation from Tatoeba (CC BY 2.0 FR).
exercises.prompt: The constant border wars between England and Scotland came to an end.

exercises.why: **подойти́** — **подходи́ть** — to approach, to come to, to walk to, to draw near .mw-parser-output .object-usage-tag{font-style:italic}.mw-parser-output .deprecated{color:var(--wikt-palette-grey-lime-8,olivedrab)}[with к (k)]; to fit, to suit, to match, to be right [with dative]. **подъе́хать** — **подъезжа́ть** — to drive up (to); (colloquial) to drop in, to pay a short visit. **подлете́ть** — **подлета́ть** — to fly up (to), to approach; (colloquial) to run/rush up (to). — DLI, Lesson 29.  ·  From Антон Чехов, «В родном углу».

exercises.why: The verb **написать** is called perfective and expresses a single action with emphasis on its completion (either in the past or in the future, since the present tense deals only with actions in progress). — From the DLI Grammar Reference Book, Lesson 37.  ·  From Пётр Боборыкин, «Китай-город».
exercises.context: The verb **написать** is called perfective and expresses a single action with emphasis on its completion (either in the past or in the future, since the present tense deals only with actions in progress).
